--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.complement()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Return the complement of the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.complement()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Return the complement of the graph. title: >- [Graph.complement()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Return the complement of the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the complement of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L48411-L48506){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.complement() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Complement](../assets/graphs/complement.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A four-node path A, B, C, D. In the complement every pair that was not connected becomes an accent edge (A to C, A to D, B to D), while the three original edges are dropped and shown dashed." width="100%"} Creates a new graph with the same nodes but complementary edges. An edge exists in the complement if and only if it does *not* exist in the original graph. Self-loops are never included. New edges have no attributes and default weight (`1.0` for weighted graphs). For directed graphs, complements directed edges independently in each direction. For undirected graphs, complements undirected edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph with complementary edge set. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~maximum_clique`) : The largest clique, an independent set of the original. [](`~maximum_independent_set`) : The largest set of nodes with no edges between them. [](`~line_graph`) : The graph of which edges share an endpoint. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The complement joins every pair that wasn't joined and drops every pair that was. A four-node path has 3 of the 6 possible edges, so its complement has the other 3: ::: {#be40bd42 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) others = path.complement() others.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A--C', 'A--D', 'B--D'] ``` ::: ::: Directed graphs are complemented per direction, so a missing `B -> A` is added even though `A -> B` exists: ::: {#6a0d8e11 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} one_way = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B")], directed=True) one_way.complement().get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['B->A'] ``` ::: ::: ### Exams that can share a slot An exam timetable starts from a conflict graph: 14 courses, joined when some student takes both, so their exams can't be at the same time. Its complement joins the courses that share no students, the pairs that can sit in the same slot. Of the 91 pairs, 62 can: ::: {#ae072997 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} exams = ec.exams() compatible = exams.complement() exams.count_edges(), compatible.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (29, 62) ``` ::: ::: A group of exams can all go in one slot when every pair in it is compatible, which makes it a clique of the complement. The largest has 7 courses, half the timetable in a single slot: ::: {#e043ed5f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} slot = compatible.maximum_clique() [exams.get_label_from_id(course) for course in slot] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['Physics', 'Statistics', 'History', 'Literature', 'Psychology', 'Programming', 'Web Design'] ``` ::: ::: The conflict graph is on the left and its complement on the right, with that group of 7 highlighted in both. In the conflict graph none of them are joined; in the complement they all are: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#28df82fa .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} exams.plot( label_by="label", highlight=slot, seed=2, width=360, height=360 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
